newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lockheed role in Airbus A3XX possible - Aerospatiale.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed role in Airbus A3XX possible - Aerospatiale.

text.p: France's state-owned Aerospatiale is in talks with Lockheed Martin over possible cooperation and does not exclude a role for the U.S. company in the planned Airbus A3XX large airliner, Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot said on Monday.
"Yes, we have a strong interest in holding discussions with Lockheed Martin and Lockheed is interested in discussing with us," he told journalists in a New Year presentation.
"You cannot get enough of the right kind of partners in this sort of project..." Michot said, citing Lockheed Martin as a potential partner.
He said he had met Norman Augustine, who became Lockheed Martin chairman this month, and that another meeting with the U.S. company was planned next month.
Michot said Lockheed Martin had a gap in its product range for heavyweight planes.
He said the two companies could collaborate on building refuelling aircraft, based on derivatives of passenger aircraft from the Airbus Industrie family.
Airbus is looking for risk-sharing partners for the $8 billion A3XX project, which would break Boeing's monopoly of large capacity planes.

The A3XX family would consist of a basic 555-seater, the A3XX-100 provisionally priced at $198 million each, the longer-range A3XX-100R at $201.5 million and a stretched 656-seat A3XX-200 at $223 million. The 555-seater would enter service in 2003.
Last week Airbus, said it was in advanced negotiations with South Korean firms to part finance the A3XX.
Airbus wants to involve other companies in up to 40 percent of funding for the A3XX, which would supplement traditional financing through government launch aid and Airbus partners' own resources.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
